items.followUp: What is a chromosome, and how is it related to chromatin?

rubric.why: Chromatin is present in the nucleus as a threadlike network or material.
rubric.description: Identifies chromatin as threadlike material or a network in the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its threadlike or network form and its nuclear location.

rubric.why: Chromatin consists of DNA associated with proteins.
rubric.description: States that chromatin is made of DNA and proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both DNA and proteins as its components.

modelAnswer: Chromatin is a threadlike network of DNA and proteins present in the nucleus.

rubric.why: A prosthetic group is strongly attached to its enzyme.
rubric.description: States that a prosthetic group is tightly bound to an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its strong or lasting association with the enzyme.

rubric.why: A coenzyme associates loosely or temporarily with an enzyme.
rubric.description: States that a coenzyme is loosely or temporarily associated with an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its weaker or temporary association with the enzyme.

modelAnswer: A prosthetic group is a non-protein component tightly bound to an enzyme.
A coenzyme is an organic non-protein molecule that associates loosely or temporarily with an enzyme.
